name: Duplicate QT7.1 — Partial Duplicate (Modifier/Units/Charges Differ → Pay) Navigator
description: Resolve the PX_DP1/PX_QT7 hard edits flagging a potential duplicate whose details only partially match: confirm the LOB via Product, identify the electronic receipt method from the DCN camera reel, rule out corrected-claim events, compare the duplicate claim, verify the history claim was processed correctly, identify a partial match, compare the rendering providers, rule out the VA-Veterans-Georgia case, determine the applicable claim scenario (modifiers), note the current claim's TC modifier, consult the Modifier Review grid (TC vs 26 ⇒ not a duplicate), then pay the claim.

steps.name: Identify the PX_DP1 and PX_QT7 hard edits
steps.description: The app will display all edits in the Event Resolution tab, with the PX_DP1 and PX_QT7 hard edits highlighted with an error indication — these are the current events to resolve. PX_QT7 indicates a partial duplicate: some details differ (modifier, units, charges), so the duplicate review must be completed before deciding.
steps.hint: Open the 'Event Resolution' tab. The PX_DP1 and PX_QT7 edits are active and highlighted in red.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes as soon as the trainee opens the Event Resolution tab.
steps.checklistItem: Identify the PX_DP1 and PX_QT7 hard edits

steps.name: Check the Line of Business via Product field
steps.description: Determine whether the claim is ITS or another Line of Business (LOB) by navigating to the Member Information tab, then the Group Information section, and reviewing the Product field. For ITS claims, the Product field may display values such as Local, National, or ACA. If the Product value is not Local, follow the alternate guidelines. If the Product value is Local, proceed to the next step. In this scenario, the Product is Local; therefore, the trainee may proceed. Also determine whether the claim was received electronically (alphanumeric) or by paper (numeric) by inspecting the DCN number
steps.hint: Open 'Member Info' and read the Product field under the Group section — it reads 'Local'.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Member Info tab to read the Product field.
steps.checklistItem: Check the Line of Business via Product field

steps.name: Check for corrected claim events (PX_PAJ/PX_SCB)
steps.description: Determine whether the claim contains corrected claim events by looking for PX_PAJ or PX_SCB events in the Event Resolution tab. If corrected claim events are present, follow the corrected events guidelines; if absent, proceed. In this scenario, the claim does not contain corrected claim events, so the trainee proceeds.
steps.hint: Return to 'Event Resolution' and scan the All Edits list — there are no PX_PAJ or PX_SCB corrected-claim events.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee revisits the Event Resolution tab to rule out corrected-claim events.

steps.name: Trigger the duplicate-claim comparison
steps.description: Obtain the potential duplicate claim(s) by navigating to the Claim Data tab, then the Duplicate sub-tab. Review the list of potential duplicate claims displayed in the table. Select the applicable duplicate claim using the radio button in the first column, then click Compare Claim. Once the comparison is initiated, a new section titled Claim Compare Results will appear below the duplicates table. Within this section, review the Show Differences subsection to identify and evaluate any differences between the current claim and the selected potential duplicate claim.
steps.hint: Open Claim Data → Duplicate, select the duplicate line's radio, then click 'Compare Claim'.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee selects the duplicate radio and clicks Compare Claim (dispatches the compare_claim action).

steps.name: Confirm the claim appears to be a duplicate
steps.description: Review the Claim compare results under the Show differences section, checking Tax ID, Group or Provider name, Rendering speciality or license number, and Attachments. The basic identifiers match the history claim, so the claim is initially flagged as a duplicate — the only differences appear in the Claim Lines accordion (modifier, units, charges). Expand the accordions to confirm.
steps.hint: Expand the Claim Compare Results accordions — the basic identifiers match; only the Claim Lines accordion shows differences (modifier TC vs 26).
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee reviews the compare-results accordions (dispatches review_duplicate).
steps.checklistItem: Confirm the claim appears to be a duplicate

steps.name: Verify the history claim was processed correctly
steps.description: Determine whether the history (duplicate) claim was processed correctly. Click the Open claim detail button to open the history claim. The system displays a message: "In real application, you need to follow guidelines to check if the history claim is processed correctly. In this scenario, consider this history claim is processed correctly." If the history claim was processed incorrectly, it must be adjusted before proceeding; if it was processed correctly, proceed. In this scenario, the history claim is processed correctly, so the trainee proceeds.
steps.hint: Click 'Open Claim Detail' on the history claim, read the advisory message, then proceed.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the history claim detail pop-up (dispatches open_claim_detail).
steps.checklistItem: Verify the history claim was processed correctly

steps.name: Identify a partial match
steps.description: Compare claim information between the current claim and the history claim across all relevant fields: Tax ID, Group or Provider name, Rendering speciality or license number, Attachments, Date of service, Place of treatment, Procedure code, Modifiers, Diagnosis codes, National Drug Codes, Billed amount, and Units of occurrence. Note the values of these fields from both claims so you can compare them. To view them side by side, click Confirm match — the values from both the current claim and the history claim will be listed for review. If all fields match exactly, treat as a duplicate; if information only partially matches, proceed to deeper review. In this scenario, the information only partially matches (modifier, units, and charges differ), so the trainee proceeds.
steps.hint: Open the Matching Duplicate Information panel — the Modifier (TC vs 26), Units and Billed amount differ, so this is only a partial match.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee confirms the matching-field list and sees the partial match (dispatches review_matching).

steps.name: Note the current claim's rendering speciality
steps.description: Determine whether the rendering speciality on the current claim and the history claim are different. First, note the rendering speciality on the current claim. Go to the Provider Information tab and, under the Rendering section, check the Specialty Description. In this scenario, the Specialty Description is DIAGNOSTIC RADIOLOGY.
steps.hint: Open Provider Info → Rendering and read the Speciality description — it reads 'DIAGNOSTIC RADIOLOGY'.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Provider Info tab to read the current claim's rendering Speciality description.
steps.checklistItem: Note the current claim's rendering provider

steps.name: Review the history claim's rendering speciality
steps.description: Now check the rendering speciality on the history claim. Navigate to the Search tab → Claims sub-tab and click Search. The history claim is listed as a summary showing its details — Code, Name, From, To, Type, Provider, Bill Type, DCN, Charged, Paid, and Status. Directly below this summary, click the Open Claim Detail button. The history claim opens in the same layout as the current claim. Under the Rendering section of the Provider Information tab, note the Specialty Description — here it is RADIATION ONCOLOGY. Because the rendering providers are different, verify whether all of the remaining criteria match: same Tax ID, same Provider Group, same Specialty/Subspecialty, same Date of Service, same Procedure Code, same Billed Amount, and no modifier or the same modifier (line level). In this scenario, the rendering-provider specialties differ (Diagnostic Radiology vs Radiation Oncology), so the criteria do not fully match — continue to the next step.
steps.hint: Open Search → Claims, click Search, then click 'Open Claim Detail' on the history claim — its rendering Speciality description is 'RADIATION ONCOLOGY', so the specialties differ.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee clicks 'Open Claim Detail' on the history claim in Search → Claims (dispatches the open_prior_claim action).
steps.checklistItem: Review the history claim's rendering provider

steps.name: Check for VA Veterans Administration in Georgia
steps.description: Determine whether the claim was submitted by a VA Veterans Administration facility located in Georgia by navigating to the Provider Information tab, then the Billing section, and reviewing the Name field. Verify that the provider name displayed on the claim matches the provider name shown in the system. Claims submitted by a VA Veterans Administration facility will typically display a VA-related provider name. Next, review the National State field in the same Billing section to confirm the provider's state. If the provider is a VA Veterans Administration facility and the National State is GA (Georgia), follow the applicable guidelines. If either condition is not met, proceed to the next step. In this scenario, the Name field displays BEVERLY RADIOLOGY MEDICAL and the National State is CA; therefore, the claim is not from a VA Veterans Administration facility in Georgia, and the trainee may proceed to the next step.
steps.hint: Open Provider Info → Billing — the Name is 'BEVERLY RADIOLOGY MEDICAL' and the National State is 'CA', so this is not a VA Veterans hospital in Georgia.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Provider Info tab to check the billing name and national state.
steps.checklistItem: Check for VA Veterans Administration in Georgia

steps.name: Determine the claim scenario and note the current claim's modifier (TC)
steps.description: Determine which claim scenario applies — Surgeries, Modifiers, ACA California HMO Encounter, QCM event, Ambulance, Procedure code 62270, or Administration services (90460-90461) with SOP document. In this scenario, the claim qualifies for the "Either of the claims contain modifiers" scenario, so it proceeds to the Modifier review. On the Claim Lines tab, review the modifiers present on the current claim — in this scenario, the current claim carries TC as the modifier.
steps.hint: Open the 'Claim Lines' tab and read the Modifiers field — the current claim carries the TC modifier, so the 'Either of the claims contain modifiers' scenario applies.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Claim Lines tab to confirm the modifiers scenario and note the TC modifier.
steps.checklistItem: Determine the claim scenario and note the current claim's modifier (TC)

steps.name: Compare modifiers via the Modifier Review grid
steps.description: Identify the history claim's modifier by navigating to the Claim Data tab, then the Duplicate sub-tab, and reviewing the Claim Compare Results section. Note the modifier associated with the related claim. In this scenario, the related claim contains modifier 26. Next, use the Modifiers Duplicate Review Excel – Determine Duplicate grid to evaluate whether the current claim should be considered a duplicate. Because both claims are billed under the same rendering specialty, use the first worksheet of the grid. Compare the modifiers for the current and related claims. In this scenario, the current claim contains modifier TC and the related claim contains modifier 26. Based on the guidance in the grid, this modifier combination indicates that the current claim should not be considered a duplicate. Therefore, the trainee may proceed to the next step.
steps.hint: Open Claim Data → Duplicate and review the claim comparison — TC (current) vs 26 (history) by the same rendering provider ⇒ first sheet ⇒ not a duplicate. Proceed to pay.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Claim Data → Duplicate sub-tab to compare the modifiers (TC vs 26).
steps.checklistItem: Compare modifiers via the Modifier Review grid

steps.name: Submit the Pay decision
steps.description: Navigate to the Decision section in the header, select 'Pay' from the dropdown menu and click Submit to finalize the Pay decision and complete the attempt.
steps.hint: In the Decision section, select 'Pay' and click Submit.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee submits the Pay decision with the Submit button.
